label: DEL / late first-occurrence c,a,2,0,k in sequences that open with 3/g/m/e/x/t/b/v
explanation: Fires almost only before the copy phase: about 55% of activation mass is on the <DEL> step (7x lift) and about 45% on late original-phase steps (t>=3; rate rises with t and L), mostly when the input is a first occurrence of c, a, 2, 0 or k. Essentially never fires in the copy phase or at t<2. What gates it is which tokens opened the sequence: activity is much higher when at least two of the first three original tokens come from {3,g,m,e,x,t,b,v} (first_tok and next_out lifts of 3-5x). The top examples begin with tokens like 3 3 m, t g g, m m g. This is a conjunction over hidden-state content, not a clean single-token detector. Precision is only about 0.3: many <DEL> steps with matching openings stay inactive, so it depends on more of the prefix than this captures. I did not check magnitude beyond seeing that coverage rises in the top activation quartile.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: in_tok=c (+5.88), in_tok=a (+4.59), in_tok=2 (+3.99), in_tok=0 (+3.49), in_tok=k (+3.38), in_tok=d (+2.82). Lower it: phase=2 (-9.61), orig0=a (-3.90), orig0=n (-3.72), orig0=2 (-3.71).
